page: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a dual-accelerator cloud GPU instance designed for compute-heavy parallel workloads, machine learning inference, and high-throughput data processing. Powered by 32 dedicated physical cores from an Intel Xeon 6448H processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, the system operates on the x86_64 architecture with one thread per core and hardware vector support including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, and BF16). It is provisioned with 375 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory allocation of approximately 11.72 GB per core, coupled with 2200 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Hardware acceleration is anchored by two NVIDIA L40S Ada Lovelace GPUs providing an aggregate of 96 GB of GDDR6 VRAM (48 GB per GPU). In benchmark evaluations, this graphics architecture excels in model inference, achieving top-tier performance of 13,643.47 tokens per second for prompt processing and 348.06 tokens per second for generation on small 135M parameter models. For medium 7B models, throughput sustains 6,275.36 prompt tokens per second and 141.42 generation tokens per second. Host compute matches this accelerator density, posting a PassMark CPU score of 64,768.69 and multi-core stress-ng metric of 62,892.75.

The balance between dense accelerator capacity, broad vector instruction sets, and large host memory makes the instance resource-efficient for mid-tier AI training, fine-tuning, real-time LLM inference serving, high-fidelity rendering, and high-throughput database caching workloads like Redis.

Potential tradeoffs involve memory write bandwidth, which registers at an average 88.2 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, and base CPU clock speeds of 2.0 GHz which prioritize multi-core parallelism over raw single-threaded frequency. It serves primarily as a deployment platform for generative AI, text-to-image pipelines, LLM inference endpoints, ray tracing simulations, and large-scale data science pipelines.
description: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is an accelerator-focused instance tailored for deep learning inference, 3D rendering, and parallelized scientific computing. Driven by 32 dedicated Intel Xeon 6448H cores operating at 2.0 GHz on x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 extensions, the system includes 375 GB of host memory and 2200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Graphics acceleration is powered by dual NVIDIA L40S Ada Lovelace GPUs delivering a total of 96 GB VRAM. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates exceptional AI throughput, reaching 6,275.36 prompt tokens per second and 141.42 text generation tokens per second on 7B LLM models, alongside strong multi-core PassMark scores of 64,768.69. The combination of dense host memory, rapid local NVMe, and dual enterprise GPUs provides high operational capability without the platform costs of multi-node clusters, making it suitable for LLM deployment, media processing, and batch analytics.
